review_comments: that seems like it should be on the serializer options in the long term?
oh, I see this is the default for the Default options?
are there tests for invalid configuration as well? (is that even possible?)
It's not possible for the new option to be set improperly (it just controls if non-optional ctor params should be required). But perhaps you mean something different?

Because I've updated the error message so that property names are wrapped with single quotes, I'm also increasing the cutoff so that roughly speaking the same number of properties are being displayed.

Can you please explain why `!IsMemberInitializer` makes this evaluate as false?

From its remarks, what's an object initialize expression?
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/60edbf9371ff00349e9224fb0920c8bca51f1a4f/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/Metadata/JsonParameterInfo.cs#L81-L82

It is members initialized via [object initializer expressions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/programming-guide/classes-and-structs/object-and-collection-initializers#object-initializers). In the case of the source generator, `required` or `init` members can only be specified as object initializers so they are included as secondary parameters in the generated constructor delegate, roughly:
```C#
args => new MyPoco(args[0], args[1]) { RequiredProp = args[2], InitProp = args[3] };
```
The second type of parameters are identified by the `IsMemberInitializer` property.

For the case of this feature, we are only interested in non-optional parameters that are not initializers (because requiredness is handled differently in that case).
should you also be checking for HasDefaultValue here?
The `IsRequiredParameter` is a composite property that takes that into account (as well as the global `options` setting)
I'd appreciate tests around this being properly/incorrectly configured (or did I miss it somehow?)

Even though the `JsonParameterInfo` has been made public for use by JSON schema, the public APIs are read-only. From a contract customization perspective the mutable API surface remains the same. In https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/102499 and https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/102902 I added a few tests checking that this API surface is properly invalidated (e.g. in cases where properties are removed or the constructor delegate is replaced).

Unless you mean somebody setting incorrect values in the [parameter models used by the source generator](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.json.serialization.metadata.jsonparameterinfovalues?view=net-8.0)? We've never validated those, which is probably ok since they're marked `EditorBrowsable.Never`.
